extra.explanation: China is exporting its way through weak domestic demand, with a nine-month trade surplus near $938 billion. That means cheaper Chinese EVs, steel and solar in other markets, and more tariffs in response.
options: More price pressure from cheap Chinese goods, and more trade friction
Less competition as China focuses on its home market
Higher Chinese demand for their finished goods
A much stronger yuan that makes Chinese goods expensive
extra.prompt: China's September exports jumped about 36%. What is the most likely effect on manufacturers in other countries?

extra.explanation: Higher inflation keeps the Fed from cutting and pushes long-term yields up. With 30-year mortgages near 7.4%, builder confidence fell to its lowest since 2012 and 43% of builders cut prices.
options: Builders use oil as their main raw material
It pushes home prices up too fast for buyers
It keeps interest rates, and so mortgage rates, high, which freezes demand
Gasoline taxes are added to home prices
extra.prompt: Why does oil-driven inflation hurt US homebuilders?

extra.explanation: Contract rates are fixed for the year, while diesel rose about 68% since before the Iran war. Surcharges recover part of that cost, but late, so carriers are cutting maintenance and delaying new trucks.
options: Freight volumes fell to almost nothing
Their rates were set before fuel rose, and fuel surcharges only pass costs on with a lag
Regulators capped trucking rates
Driver wages fell sharply
extra.prompt: Truckers on fixed annual contracts are losing money with diesel near $6.30. Why?

extra.explanation: With revenue down 15% and paying users down 16%, Bumble needs time to rework its product. Private ownership lets it experiment without reporting to public investors every quarter.
options: To raise cheaper equity from the public
Regulators required it
To pay a large special dividend to public shareholders
To restructure and rebuild the product without quarterly public-market pressure
extra.prompt: Bumble is going private at $1.3B, down from roughly $14B at its IPO. What is the usual main reason a board chooses a take-private in this situation?

extra.explanation: Drug sales grew about 8% and outpaced devices. Separating slower units, as J&J did with Kenvue in 2023, lets each business be valued and run on its own terms.
options: Focus capital and management on higher-margin, faster-growing businesses like drugs
Avoid a patent cliff in orthopedics
Merge orthopedics into Kenvue
Exit healthcare altogether
extra.prompt: J&J is leaning toward spinning off its orthopedics unit. What is the main strategic logic?

questions.explanation: Hormuz tanker transits are running about 70% below pre-war levels. The oil exists but can't move safely, so freight, insurance and the physical premium drive the price. OPEC+ doesn't meet until Nov 1.
options: OPEC+ announced a large production cut
Attacks on shipping mean Gulf oil can't safely get through the Strait of Hormuz
US shale output fell sharply this quarter
Chinese oil demand surged on a strong recovery
questions.prompt: Brent is near $110 even though the world's oil reserves haven't changed. What is the main reason?

questions.explanation: An exporter buys gas near $3, liquefies and ships it, and sells near $29. That spread is the margin. European and Asian buyers pay the high price, and US households just see normal domestic prices.
options: European factories that use gas
Japanese utilities buying cargoes on the spot market
US LNG exporters with cargoes to sell
US households heating with gas
questions.prompt: US gas (Henry Hub) is about $3/MMBtu while Asian spot LNG is about $29. Who captures the most value from that gap?

questions.explanation: CoreWeave rents GPUs under contracts concentrated in a few customers and funded its fleet largely with debt. If those customers spend less, revenue and debt service are both at risk, which is why it fell 25%+ in last week's sell-off.
options: A debt-funded AI cloud provider with a few very large customers, like CoreWeave
A payment network like Visa
A consumer staples company like Procter & Gamble
A large US bank
questions.prompt: Which kind of company is most exposed if big tech firms cut their AI data center spending?

questions.explanation: Proofpoint sells email security and Varonis sells data security, both to corporate security chiefs. The logic is revenue synergy: sell both products to each customer. This 'platform plus add-on' approach is a classic private equity playbook.
options: Vertical integration into a supplier
A merger of two direct competitors to cut costs
Diversification into an unrelated industry
A platform company buying an adjacent product to cross-sell to the same buyers
questions.prompt: Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint is buying Varonis for $6.3B. How would you best describe the strategy?

questions.explanation: Regulators said the bank left more than $5 billion of suspicious activity unreported or reported late. The OCC's $750 million share was the largest civil penalty in its history. American Express was fined $350 million for similar failures a week earlier.
options: It failed to properly monitor and report suspicious transactions under anti-money-laundering rules
It held too little capital against its loans
It misled investors about interest rate risk
It broke consumer rules on overdraft fees
questions.prompt: Why was Bank of America hit with more than $1.2 billion in penalties?

questions.explanation: Management pointed to low imports and long lead times under the current trade environment. The flip side: automakers and other steel buyers pay more for their inputs.
options: Chinese demand for US steel surged
Iron ore became much cheaper
Trade protection keeps imports low, giving US mills pricing power
It merged with Nucor and cut capacity
questions.prompt: Cleveland-Cliffs' average steel price is up about 14% from a year ago. What is the main reason?

questions.explanation: Banks borrow cheaply through deposits and lend at higher rates. That spread, net interest income, is the largest profit line for most big banks. Fee businesses add steadier but smaller revenue.
options: Investment banking advisory fees
Net interest income: the spread between what it earns on loans and pays on deposits
Trading revenue
Late fees on credit cards
questions.prompt: For a large US bank, what is usually the single biggest source of profit?

questions.explanation: A patented drug earns very high margins until its patent expires, then sales drop sharply as generics or biosimilars arrive. Buying biotechs refills the pipeline. J&J said this week that new drug deals will weigh on its 2027 earnings.
options: To lower their manufacturing costs
To move into medical devices
To replace revenue they'll lose when patents on their blockbuster drugs expire
To reduce the taxes they pay on research
questions.prompt: Why do big pharma companies keep buying biotech companies?

questions.explanation: Lenders fund LNG projects because buyers commit to long-term contracts up front, often priced at Henry Hub times 115% plus a fixed fee. The contracts make the cash flow predictable enough to borrow against.
options: By selling cargoes on the spot market as they are produced
Mostly through government grants
Through retail bonds sold to consumers
Against long-term, roughly 20-year, offtake contracts signed before construction
questions.prompt: How is a new $10B+ LNG export terminal typically financed?

questions.explanation: New US shale wells typically need around $60 to $65 a barrel. With WTI above $100, shale producers are very profitable, but they are prioritizing dividends and buybacks over fast growth.
options: About $20 a barrel
About $60 to $65 a barrel
About $110 a barrel
About $150 a barrel
questions.prompt: Roughly what oil price do new US shale wells need to break even?
